prerequisites: Adequate knowledge and skills in fundamental mathematical tools (algebra, basic derivatives and integrals)
Production Planning and Control (Programmazione e Controllo della Produzione.)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire fundamental knowledge and the ability to interpret the characteristics and objectives of integrated logistics in production and distribution systems.
Gain knowledge of the principles of classification of production systems, warehouses, and both traditional and advanced logistic equipment (e.g., AGVs, automated warehouses).
Acquire a basic understanding of the strategic role of packaging and container standardization in logistics decision-making.
Develop knowledge of production information flows, with particular reference to MRP, JIT, and kanban systems.
Understand the key concepts related to the impact of production layout on logistics performance and the principles of flexible design.
Develop the ability to analyze and design layouts and material handling systems consistent with different production and distribution typologies.
Acquire the ability to evaluate and select packaging and load unit solutions aimed at improving logistics flow efficiency.
Apply methods and tools for material requirements planning and production scheduling.
Develop practical skills in sizing logistics systems (warehouses, AGVs, FMS, assembly lines), taking into account both technical and economic aspects.
Acquire the ability to evaluate the performance of a logistics system in terms of flexibility, efficiency, and costs, and to propose appropriate improvements.
Identify the interconnections between logistics management, layout design, service level, and economic–environmental sustainability.
Acquire the ability to prepare technical reports on the design and evaluation of material handling and storage systems.
Present the results of logistics analyses and simulations, justifying design choices and their operational and economic impacts.
Develop the ability to communicate effectively using technical and professional terminology within the field of logistics systems management.
Acquire the ability to integrate logistics knowledge with other subjects within the degree program (production, maintenance, safety, sustainability).

Develop the capacity to use the acquired methods and techniques as a foundation for further study and professional development, with a particular focus on innovative and digital technologies for Logistics 4.0 and 5.0.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Integrated and Flexible Logistics
Evolution of Production Systems and Enabling Technologies
Layout and Design of Logistics Systems
Information Flow Management and Production Planning

assessment_methods.method: Written examination of the content of the lectures and exercise sessions
Two partial written intermediate evaluation tests

assessment_rules: The student's proficiency is tested through a written examination covering the whole syllabus. During the course, there will be two partial written intermediate evaluation tests. The test is passed if the student receives a rating of at least 18/30 in both parts. The final vote is the arithmetic average of the two partial written tests (rounded up). Those who are not satisfied with the marks obtained in partial examinations may repeat the written test, which annuls previous results. The grade of 18/30 is awarded for elementary knowledge/skills, and 30/30 cum laude for excellent knowledge.
bibliography: S. Chopra, P. Meindl, "Supply Chain Management - Strategy, Planning, and Operation", Pearson.
Persona, Pareschi, Ferrari, Regattieri, "Logistica integrata e flessibile", Esculapio.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Meccanica E Gestionale (First Level Degree In Mechanical And Management Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
